Subject: Production latency spike - us-west-2 AZ1

Hi Laura / Redwood support,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and increasing 5xx rate across our production traffic in us-west-2 (AZ1) starting ~07:50 PDT. Throughput has dropped ~40% and our app errors are cascading to downstream customers. We attached a minimal capture from our side (request IDs + sample traces).

Attachments: catalyst_error_snaps.zip (sample trace + request ids)

-Dana

Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike - us-west-2 AZ1 — initial findings

Forwarding initial debug notes. Summary:
- Observed elevated tail latency and 5xxs from a subset of AZ1 workers serving Catalyst's dedicated pool.
- Memory pressure + kernel preemption caused a small subset of model workers to drop requests; KV-cache misses spiked (likely due to an alignment of large context requests).
- Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because we hit an API quota check while a fallback health probe was running.

Attached: usw2-inflight-logs-20280722.txt (server-side logs), sample request ids correlating to Dana's traces.

Recommendation (urgent): open an emergency circuit-breaker to stop sending new sessions to the affected AZ1 and force a cross-region reroute to our healthy us-east-1 pool for Catalyst. This is a short-lived containment play; we then rehydrate AZ1 workers with a controlled drain and redeploy optimized kernel patch.

Risks: cross-region reroute will increase RTT for some sessions (p95 may go up ~80-120ms) and could increase egress cost for Catalyst until we revert routing. Need exec sign-off for immediate emergency capacity/overage clearance.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Laura / team —
We will execute the containment play now. Plan:
1) Trigger emergency circuit-breaker for Catalyst's routing policy in us-west-2 to stop new allocations to AZ1.
2) Programmatic steering to us-east-1 with a short-lived global override (TTL 30m).
3) Spin up 4 additional dedicated workers in us-east-1 (hot standby) and bump autoscale buffer for Catalyst's pool.
4) Controlled drain of impacted AZ1 workers, apply kernel alignment patch, validate KV-cache hit rates.

Estimated time to visible customer improvement: 10–20 minutes after circuit-breaker flip. Cost note: immediate overage (~$2.5k/hr) while warm capacity spins up — this will be billed per our overage policy; recommend we apply a good-faith credit after remediation.

I'll coordinate the flip and post a timestamped entry to the incident log. Ben / Rishi: take point on validation checks. Marissa: stand ready for customer comms.

-Jonas
